1:_: (1) [seif 1] A place that has 3 partitions, etc. In Tur he wrote that from the Torah it is complete reshut hayachid and Beit Yosef wrote on it that he does not mean to obligate one who throws from reshut harabbim into it, but rather to permit carrying in all of it — for such is the law of karmelis from the Torah, as Rambam's words in chapters 14 and 17; but there are those who disagree and say a place with 3 partitions is complete reshut hayachid to obligate one who throws from reshut harabbim into it, and Maggid Mishneh already explained in chapter 17 that their dispute depends on the sugya in Eruvin 11a and 14b — see there. But Bach wrote that Tur's view is not as Rambam but to obligate also one who throws from reshut harabbim into it — see there; and so the Taz s.k. 1 except he wrote to distinguish: if open to reshut harabbim and many push into it he is not obligated for one who throws into it from reshut harabbim, and if not many push into it it is complete reshut hayachid — see there; and Eliyah Rabbah brought it ot 1 and wrote that from Bach and Magen Avraham it appears in every case he is liable; and so Chacham Tzvi Meiratayim ot 1 that from Tur's silence it appears in every case he is liable — see there; and so Nishmat Shabbos. And the essence of this law is Rashi's view on Eruvin 12b and he disagreed in several places and Ra'avad in hasagot and Rosh first chapter of Sukkah and Rashba in his commentary and Avodat HaKodesh and Ritva that with 3 partitions or with 2 partitions and lechi it is complete reshut hayachid from the Torah; and see above siman 358 ot 5 and siman 356 ot 3 and examine:
2:_: (2) There. The Sages forbade carrying in it. More than 4 amot — a decree because of reshut harabbim since it resembles it. Levush. Razah ot 1.
3:_: (3) There. The Sages forbade carrying in it. Whether breached to reshut harabbim or breached to karmelis. Razah there.
4:_: (4) There. The Sages forbade, etc. And since repair is needed only rabbinically they permitted it with any repair. Tur. Levush.
5:_: (5) There. Until some repair is made, etc. Repair of tzurat hapetach helps from the side of being complete reshut hayachid as written in Tosafos Eruvin 6a s.v. Rav and there 22a s.v. vehah amar R' Yehuda and in Rosh chapter 1 of Sukkah siman 34; but repair of korah helps only rabbinically as written in Tosafos Eruvin 6a s.v. korah; and see there Tosafos 5b s.v. shepartzato where they wrote we learn from Sinai that it helps for a mavo with lechi and korah and in a courtyard a pas 4; and see there Hagahot Chavot Shalom who wondered on this and see there Maharsha what he wrote on this; and see there Rosh chapter 8 siman 7 and Ritva 86 that for a korah 4 wide it is a partition from the Torah and for less than 4 only rabbinically because of recognition. Avodat HaKodesh ot 1 and see above siman 362 ot 88.
6:_: (6) Lechi is by reason of partition from the Torah and korah is by reason of recognition; and Eruvin 12 — a mavo they permitted with lechi: one who throws into it is liable; with korah exempt — for Rambam this is explained with 3 partitions and for other poskim with 2 partitions. And there is a practical difference for disqualification of testimony or a mumar who desecrates Shabbat — desecration of Shabbat from the Torah makes him a mumar for the entire Torah; however some say we have no reshut harabbim — see siman 358 in Taz s.k. 6. Shevut Yaakov ot 1 and see in our words there seif 7; and further practical difference if he desecrated Shabbat with a Torah prohibition or rabbinic regarding repair; and see simanim 334.
7:_: (7) [seif 2] A courtyard breached in its full, etc. to the forbidden place. Beit Yosef in the name of R' Yehonatan. Levush. See there ot 2 — meaning it breached to reshut harabbim or karmelis as written above ot 3.
8:א: (8) There. A courtyard breached in its full, etc. Explanation: in a square courtyard breached on the fourth side repair is needed different from what they repair for a mavo — its length exceeds its width and breached on the fourth side: in a courtyard a pas 4 on one side or two pasin of mashehu is needed; but in a mavo whose length exceeds its width and breached on the fourth side they permitted with lechi all that it is from one side as written below seif 3 Bach; and the same a courtyard whose length exceeds its width — its law is as a mavo as written below seif 27; and the reason for the difference between courtyard and mavo is that whatever is used discreetly requires more partition as Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Rashba; and so Razah ot 3 and see below ot 164.
8:ב: (8) There. In its full. Meaning the entire wall.
9:_: (9) There. Up to 10 amot it is permitted with a pas, etc. And although up to 10 we consider it as an opening as written above siman 362 seif 9 — here is different since it breached in its full it is stricter.
10:_: (10) There. It is permitted with a pas, etc. And all the more with tzurat hapetach as written at the end of the seif, and only if it is less than 4 tefachim one does not repair it through tzurat hapetach as written above siman 362 end of ot 94 — see there.
11:_: (11) There. It is permitted with a pas, etc. And if it is of asheirah its law is as a korah of asheirah which is invalid as written seif 16. Tosafot Shabbos ot 2 and see below ot 100.
12:_: (12) There. Two pasin of two mashehuin suffice. Shulchan Aruch distinguishes: if made by hand two mashehuin suffice, and if something remained specifically a tefach from here and a tefach from here as written afterward; and Bach wrote one should not be lenient, for even when made by hand one should make a tefach l'chatchila from here and from here — see there; however Eliyah Rabbah ot 2 challenged Bach and so is the view of the later authorities; and see below ot 14.
13:_: (13) There. In one place. Meaning at the head of the wall — for otherwise the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it as written below seif 34; and even if that remainder is 4 wide it is not nullified from the law of pas. Tosafos Eruvin 5b s.v. eino. Gra.
14:_: (14) There. A tefach from here and a tefach from here. So too Beit Yosef in the name of R' Yehonatan except he wrote on it that not specifically a tefach, for mashehu from here and mashehu from here suffices; and Tosafot Shabbos ot 4 wrote that thus explicitly in R' Yehonatan's language that Beit Yosef brought siman 372, and what he did not write thus in Shulchan Aruch — one must say he retracted and was strict as Tosafos' view — see there; and so in Darkei Moshe ot 1 he challenged Beit Yosef and wrote that in what remained specifically width of a tefach is required — see there; and so Razah ot 2; however in Rambam chapter 15 law 12 he wrote that in what remained also all that it is from here and all that it is from here suffices; and so Ritva Eruvin 16 and Peri Chadash there; and so Levush; and Eliyah Rabbah brought it ot 2 and wrote that thus everywhere in Avodat HaKodesh for Rashba 6 and it is fit to rely on Rashba's ruling — see there; and Chayei Adam klal 91 ot 3 and Nishmat Adam there ot 1 wrote that l'chatchila one should be concerned and forbid until a tefach remains, and in time of need one can rely on the lenient authorities that in what remained mashehu suffices — see there; and it appears thus one should rule for the law:
15:_: (15) There. And all this in height 19. Meaning they need not be the full height of the wall but height 19 suffices, but not less for then it has no name of partition.
16:_: (16) There. And even if there is not in the breach 4 tefachim. And it is possible he speaks of a courtyard wide in its middle and at its end it is narrow so that in its full width there is not 4 tefachim; but if the entire courtyard is less than 4 tefachim no repair is needed as written in seif 28. Magen Avraham s.k. 1; and Shevut Shmuel wrote on it that not because it is light from what is written in seif 28 that certainly there is a difference between mavo and courtyard as explained in the Gemara, but rather he means it is possible what we say in the Gemara that in a courtyard even less than 4 — this is in width in the middle and in such a case Ritva wrote law 12 — see there; and see Eliyah Rabbah ot 3.
17:_: (17) There. Since it is in its full it needs repair. And the same if not in its full it needs repair if the breach exceeds the standing as written in siman 362 seif 9.
18:_: (18) There. Until there is in it less than 3. For then even if in its full no repair is needed because of lavod.
19:_: (19) There. Even if not in its full, etc. It appears he means not only if in its full and more than 10 that it needs repair with tzurat hapetach, but even if not in its full — since it is more than 10 it needs repair with tzurat hapetach; and although according to Rambam tzurat hapetach does not help for a breach more than 10 unless standing exceeds the breach as written above siman 362 seif 10 — we already wrote there ot 95 that for width 3 even for Rambam it helps — see there.
20:_: (20) There. Even if not in its full, etc. And although something remained built from the wall about 10 — for more than 10 it does not help at all and it is as if the entire wall fell and the courtyard is forbidden to carry within until tzurat hapetach is made for that courtyard. Beit Yosef in the name of R' Yehonatan.
21:_: (21) There. Even if not in its full. Rather gippufin remained from here and from here — and even if the gippufin exceed the breach it needs repair with tzurat hapetach as written in siman 362 whether in a courtyard or mavo. Razah ot 4.
22:_: (22) [seif 3] A mavo that has 3 partitions, etc. And if it has only 2 partitions its law is explained below siman 364:
23:_: (23) There. They permitted with lechi, etc. Meaning although in a courtyard a pas 4 or two pasin of mashehu is required, in a mavo lechi all that it is suffices. See there ot 3 and the reason for the difference between courtyard and mavo see above end of ot 8.
24:_: (24) There. They permitted with lechi, etc. There is no concern of transgression in repairing mavo'ot, God forbid — on the contrary the diligent one is praiseworthy; and one may wonder on one who could repair and does not repair; and were it not for the burden of study it is the way of a Torah scholar to repair; and one whose heart strikes him on this is a complete layman or apostasy has been cast into him. Rashbatz in responsum part 2 siman 37. Berkei Yosef ot 2 and see below siman 366 ot 123:
25:_: (25) There. All that it is. Even less than a finger. Beit Yosef, Bach. Magen Avraham s.k. 2. Eliyah Rabbah ot 4. Tosafot Shabbos ot 6.
26:_: (26) There. That he place it at the opening of the mavo. At one of the walls. Razah ot 1.
27:_: (27) There. That he place it at the opening of the mavo. And if he placed it in the middle of the mavo see below seif 31.
28:_: (28) There. Its height 19. Spaced and not constricted as written below seif 26.
29:_: (29) There. Its height 19. And even if the height of the mavo is above 20 amot it is permitted with lechi height 19; and they did not say it should not be above 20 amot except for korah as written below seif 26 — see there.
30:_: (30) There. {Rama: And even if one tied a person there, etc.} He speaks where they did not inform him that they placed it for lechi — if so he will certainly leave and not stand there all day, therefore we require tied. Magen Avraham s.k. 3 and it appears if they informed him tying is not needed; and it is strained — why this trouble, better he should inform him; and it further appears that here informing does not help lest he forget and leave and tilt himself so it is not 19 high — siman 362 seif 5 speaks for a time that then we are not concerned for this. Tosafot Shabbos ot 7 and Eliyah Rabbah brought it ot 3; however Razah ot 5 wrote that if they informed him he stands for lechi we are not concerned he will leave, except then he must place it from erev Shabbat since lechi is judged as partition and it is forbidden to make a partition from a person on Shabbat unless without his knowledge as written in siman 362 seif 5, end of his words; and see there seif 3 and below seif 11:
31:_: (31) [seif 4] If there is some wall, etc. And although it was not made for lechi — it is light, for lechi standing by itself is valid as below seif 11 — see there:
32:_: (32) There. Provided there is in it width of a tefach. And although he wrote lechi all that it is suffices — this is for lechi standing by itself; but if attached to the wall it is not recognizable unless it is a tefach wide. See there ot 4 — this is according to what Shulchan Aruch wrote in seif 2 to distinguish between made by hand and what remained in the wall; however we already wrote there ot 14 that some say even in what remained all that it is suffices — if so the same here; and what Levush wrote to distinguish between there and here — Tosafot Shabbos ot 4 already challenged see there; however we already wrote there that l'chatchila one should forbid in less than a tefach as Shulchan Aruch's view and his followers — if so the same here:
33:_: (33) There. Width of a tefach. And the same for tzurat hapetach in what remained we require a tefach. Tosafot Shabbos end of ot 16; however Sha'arei Teshuvah below on seif 26 wrote on Tosafot Shabbos's words there that it is not compelled — see there:
34:_: (34) There. Width of a tefach. And it appears if this lechi is made of asheirah wood it is invalid, for since this lechi requires the measure of a tefach it is comparable to korah (below seif 16) made of asheirah wood which is invalid because since it requires the measure of a tefach we say crushing diminishes its measure — if so the same for this lechi. Tosafot Shabbos ot 8:
35:_: (35) [seif 5] A lechi that if wind blows in it, etc. And this is because we say any partition that cannot stand in a normal wind is not a partition — and the same for lechi. Beit Yosef. See there ot 5; and even if the wind does not knock it down but only shakes it it is invalid as Maharshal siman 362 wrote, Magen Avraham s.k. 4; and this means if wind blows it nullifies the partition — if not one could say it is valid. Tosafot Shabbos ot 9. Eliyah Rabbah ot 4:
36:_: (36) There. A lechi that if wind blows in it, etc. And the same for tzurat hapetach, Tosafot Shabbos there; and see there what he wrote to challenge the Taz s.k. 4 who wrote to distinguish on this — see there; and see above siman 362 ot 112:
